adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:317 — In deleteEvent the fallback `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` runs only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it always returns undefined and deletion silently targets "primary"; the resulting 404 is swallowed and cancel reports success while the event stays on the real calendar.

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `GoogleCalendarService.deleteEvent`, the new fallback branch is:

```ts
const calendarId = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

This `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (e.g. `undefined`/`null`), so it effectively searches for a destination calendar whose `externalId` equals `undefined`/`null`, which will almost always return `undefined`. That means `calendarId` will be `undefined` in the fallback case, and the delete call will not target the intended destination calendar (likely falling back elsewhere to `primary` or causing a wrong/failed deletion depending on the surrounding code). The core issue (the fallback can never select a real calendar when `externalCalendarId` is missing) is directly verifiable from the diff.

The additional claim about “404 is swallowed and cancel reports success” depends on error-handling outside this snippet, but the primary defect in calendar selection logic is real.
